title: Salad leaf bowls with crispy pork and apple

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a basic condiment such as cider vinegar and wholegrain mustard.

supermarket.reason: Pork shoulder, new potatoes, salad leaves, apples and radishes are everyday Tesco items.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a roasting tray, a knife and bowls, and the technique is simple roasting and tossing.

works.reason: Step 4 tosses 250g of delicate salad leaves straight into a tray just out of a 220°C oven with hot oily juices, so the hero leaves will collapse into a soggy wilted mass. They should be dressed in the bowls, or the tray left to cool first.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is fair for halving the potatoes, cutting the pork and slicing the apples and radishes, and 20 plus 25 minutes of roasting matches the 45 printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm salad of spring leaves, radishes, new potatoes and stored apples suits early April, and the leaves are given in a generous quantity.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a neighbour could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Pork, potatoes, leaves, apple and radish make a balanced, filling lunch a family would happily eat again.
